Research preview / Electrochemical homeostasis v2.0

When ion gradients change, the circuit changes.

Simulate finite intracellular and extracellular Na⁺, K⁺ and Cl⁻ pools, dynamic reversal potentials, ATPase pumps, proton exchange, buffered pH and electron-transfer current during prolonged stimulation.

Exploratory, not experimentally calibrated. Values below are illustrative, not cancer-specific measurements. Pump and exchanger laws are simplified phenomenological approximations. The membrane leak current and TPMET redox reservoir are not assigned explicit tracked ionic species; ionic totals and electrical capacitor balance are reported separately. Do not infer clinical treatment response, tumour growth or apoptosis from these plots.

1 · Experimental parameters

Model parameters are editable. Changing a pump activity fraction from 1 to 0 gives a defined suppression scenario, not a pharmaceutical dose–response prediction.

Run time: 10 seconds. Numerical timestep: 0.5 ms. Enter experimental provenance in the exported hypothesis record.

2 · Simulated responses

Voltage in mV, time in seconds

3 · Conservation and checks

In a closed system (bath exchange = 0), Na⁺, K⁺ and Cl⁻ totals should remain constant. Capacitor charge balance is calculated independently. Proton equivalents use an effective buffer model and are not free hydrogen-ion concentrations.

CheckComputed result

Conserved bulk ion totals alone do not prove global electrochemical electroneutrality. The leak, redox and metabolic source terms are idealised reservoirs and must be explicitly resolved in a future electrodiffusive model.

Equations, units and scientific boundaries

Reversal potentials: Eᵢ=(RT/zᵢF)ln(cₒ/cᵢ). Membrane: Cₘ dV/dt = −(INa+IK+ICl+IH+Ileak+INaK+IVATP−ITPMET−Iapp).

Na/K pump exports 3 Na⁺ and imports 2 K⁺ per unit cycle, carrying one net outward positive charge. NHE is electroneutral, exchanging intracellular H⁺ outward for extracellular Na⁺ inward. The proton V-ATPase is treated as an outward electrogenic proton source. Ion flux changes are divided by valence, Faraday's constant and compartment volume. Cytosolic pH dynamics are based on proton equivalents divided by a constant buffering capacity.

TPMET is represented as a prescribed electrical current, not a fully specified redox pathway. Phenomenological leak current and imposed current represent electrical reservoirs; no corresponding chemical species inventories are supplied. No diffusion, mobile buffers, channel gating, ATP dynamics, electroneutrality constraints, external-field coupling, measured cancer-type parameters or tissue geometries are represented. Pump suppression is a hypothesis-generating calculation, not an estimate of drug effects.
